sanskrit: etad icchāmy ahaṃ tvattaḥ śrotuṃ bhārgavanandana kautūhalasamāviṣṭo yathātathyaṃ mahāmune
english: This I wish to hear from you, O joy of the Bhārgava line — filled with curiosity, I wish to know it exactly as it is, O great sage.

sanskrit: mārkaṇḍeya uvāca atrāpy udāharantīmam itihāsaṃ purātanam yathā kruddho hutavahas tapas taptuṃ vanaṃ gataḥ
english: Mārkaṇḍeya said: On this point too they cite this ancient tale — how Hutavaha, enraged, went to the forest to perform austerities.

sanskrit: yathā ca bhagavān agniḥ svayam evāṅgirābhavat saṃtāpayan svaprabhayā nāśayaṃs timirāṇi ca
english: And how the blessed Agni himself became Aṅgiras, scorching with his own radiance and dispelling darkness.

sanskrit: āśramastho mahābhāgo havyavāhaṃ viśeṣayan tathā sa bhūtvā tu tadā jagat sarvaṃ prakāśayan
english: Dwelling in the hermitage, the greatly blessed one surpassed Havyavāha; having become thus, he illumined the entire world.

sanskrit: tapaś caraṃś ca hutabhuk saṃtaptas tasya tejasā bhṛśaṃ glānaś ca tejasvī na sa kiṃ cit prajajñivān
english: And Hutabhuk, while performing austerities, was scorched by his heat; the radiant one, greatly afflicted, knew nothing at all.

sanskrit: atha saṃcintayām āsa bhagavān havyavāhanaḥ anyo 'gnir iha lokānāṃ brahmaṇā saṃpravartitaḥ agnitvaṃ vipranaṣṭaṃ hi tapyamānasya me tapaḥ
english: Then the blessed Havyavāhana reflected: another fire has been set in motion by Brahmā for the worlds; my fire-nature is indeed lost, for this penance torments me.

sanskrit: katham agniḥ punar ahaṃ bhaveyam iti cintya saḥ apaśyad agnival lokāṃs tāpayantaṃ mahāmunim
english: Thinking "How can I become fire again?" he saw the great sage scorching the worlds like fire itself.

sanskrit: sopāsarpac chanair bhītas tam uvāca tadāṅgirāḥ śīghram eva bhavasvāgnis tvaṃ punar lokabhāvanaḥ vijñātaś cāsi lokeṣu triṣu saṃsthānacāriṣu
english: He approached slowly, afraid, and then Aṅgiras spoke to him: "Become fire once more without delay — you who sustain the worlds; you are known in the three worlds among those who dwell in the three stations."

sanskrit: tvam agne prathamaḥ sṛṣṭo brahmaṇā timirāpahaḥ svasthānaṃ pratipadyasva śīghram eva tamonuda
english: "You, O Agni, were created first by Brahmā as the dispeller of darkness; return to your own station quickly, O destroyer of gloom."

sanskrit: agnir uvāca naṣṭakīrtir ahaṃ loke bhavāñ jāto hutāśanaḥ bhavantam eva jñāsyanti pāvakaṃ na tu māṃ janāḥ
english: Agni said: My fame is lost in the world; you have been born as Hutāśana; people will know only you as Pāvaka, not me.

sanskrit: nikṣipāmy aham agnitvaṃ tvam agniḥ prathamo bhava bhaviṣyāmi dvitīyo 'haṃ prājāpatyaka eva ca
english: "I abandon fire-hood; you become the first fire; I shall be the second, namely the Prājāpatya fire."

sanskrit: aṅgirā uvāca kuru puṇyaṃ prajāsvargyaṃ bhavāgnis timirāpahaḥ māṃ ca deva kuruṣvāgne prathamaṃ putram añjasā
english: Aṅgiras said: "Do the meritorious work that leads creatures to heaven; be the fire that dispels darkness; and O god, O Agni, make me straightway your first son."

sanskrit: mārkaṇḍeya uvāca tac chrutvāṅgiraso vākyaṃ jātavedās tathākarot rājan bṛhaspatir nāma tasyāpy aṅgirasaḥ sutaḥ
english: Mārkaṇḍeya said: Hearing the words of Aṅgiras, Jātavedas did accordingly, O king; and Bṛhaspati by name was the son of that Aṅgiras.

sanskrit: jñātvā prathamajaṃ taṃ tu vahner āṅgirasaṃ sutam upetya devāḥ papracchuḥ kāraṇaṃ tatra bhārata
english: Knowing that firstborn son of fire, the Āṅgirasa, the gods approached and asked the reason there, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: sa tu pṛṣṭas tadā devais tataḥ kāraṇam abravīt pratyagṛhṇaṃs tu devāś ca tad vaco 'ṅgirasas tadā
english: Being questioned by the gods, he then stated the reason; and the gods accepted the word of Aṅgiras at that time.

sanskrit: atra nānāvidhān agnīn pravakṣyāmi mahāprabhān karmabhir bahubhiḥ khyātān nānātvaṃ brāhmaṇeṣv iha
english: Here I shall describe the many kinds of fires, greatly luminous, known by many deeds — their multiplicity among the brāhmaṇas in this world.

sanskrit: mārkaṇḍeya uvāca brahmaṇo yas tṛtīyas tu putraḥ kurukulodvaha tasyāpavasutā bhāryā prajās tasyāpi me śṛṇu
english: Mārkaṇḍeya said: He who was the third son of Brahmā, O ornament of the Kuru lineage — his wife was Apavā; hear from me his offspring as well.

sanskrit: bṛhajjyotir bṛhatkīrtir bṛhadbrahmā bṛhanmanāḥ bṛhanmantro bṛhadbhāsas tathā rājan bṛhaspatiḥ
english: Bṛhajjyotis, Bṛhatkīrti, Bṛhadbrahmā, Bṛhanmanās, Bṛhanmantra, Bṛhadbhāsa, and likewise, O king, Bṛhaspati.

sanskrit: prajāsu tāsu sarvāsu rūpeṇāpratimābhavat devī bhānumatī nāma prathamāṅgirasaḥ sutā
english: Among all those creatures she was unrivalled in beauty — the goddess named Bhānumatī, the first daughter of Aṅgiras.

sanskrit: bhūtānām eva sarveṣāṃ yasyāṃ rāgas tadābhavat rāgād rāgeti yām āhur dvitīyāṅgirasaḥ sutā
english: She in whom passion arose in all beings at that time — she is called Rāgā from passion; she is the second daughter of Aṅgiras.

sanskrit: yāṃ kapardisutām āhur dṛśyādṛśyeti dehinaḥ tanutvāt sā sinīvālī tṛtīyāṅgirasaḥ sutā
english: She whom they call the daughter of Kapardī, "the seen and unseen" — she is Sinīvālī on account of her slenderness; she is the third daughter of Aṅgiras.

sanskrit: paśyaty arciṣmatī bhābhir havirbhiś ca haviṣmatī ṣaṣṭhīm aṅgirasaḥ kanyāṃ puṇyām āhur haviṣmatīm
english: She who sees with radiant rays and is rich in oblations — Haviṣmatī; they call the sixth holy daughter of Aṅgiras Haviṣmatī.

sanskrit: mahāmakheṣv āṅgirasī dīptimatsu mahāmatī mahāmatīti vikhyātā saptamī kathyate sutā
english: In great sacrifices the Āṅgirasī, in brilliant rites the great-minded one — known as Mahāmatī, she is spoken of as the seventh daughter.

sanskrit: yāṃ tu dṛṣṭvā bhagavatīṃ janaḥ kuhukuhāyate ekānaṃśeti yām āhuḥ kuhūm aṅgirasaḥ sutām
english: She the blessed one upon seeing whom people cry "kuhu kuhu" — her they call Ekānaṃśā; she is Kuhū, the daughter of Aṅgiras.

sanskrit: mārkaṇḍeya uvāca bṛhaspateś cāndramasī bhāryābhūd yā yaśasvinī agnīn sājanayat puṇyān ṣaḍekāṃ cāpi putrikām
english: Mārkaṇḍeya said: The illustrious lunar wife who became wife of Bṛhaspati — she bore six holy fires and one daughter as well.

sanskrit: āhutiṣv eva yasyāgner haviṣājyaṃ vidhīyate so 'gnir bṛhaspateḥ putraḥ śaṃyur nāma mahāprabhaḥ
english: That fire whose oblation of clarified butter is prescribed in the āhutis — that fire, son of Bṛhaspati, is named Śaṃyu, greatly radiant.

sanskrit: cāturmāsyeṣu yasyeṣṭyām aśvamedhe 'grajaḥ paśuḥ dīpto jvālair anekābhair agnir eko 'tha vīryavān
english: He at whose sacrifice in the Cāturmāsya rites the horse is the foremost victim — the single valiant fire blazing with many flames.

sanskrit: śaṃyor apratimā bhāryā satyā satyā ca dharmajā agnis tasya suto dīptas tisraḥ kanyāś ca suvratāḥ
english: Śaṃyu's wife was the incomparable Satyā, Satyā born of dharma; his son was Dīpta, the fire, and three virtuous daughters.

sanskrit: prathamenājyabhāgena pūjyate yo 'gnir adhvare agnis tasya bharadvājaḥ prathamaḥ putra ucyate
english: The fire who is honoured with the first share of clarified butter at the sacrifice — that fire's son is called Bharadvāja, the first.

sanskrit: paurṇamāsyeṣu sarveṣu haviṣājyaṃ sruvodyatam bharato nāmataḥ so 'gnir dvitīyaḥ śaṃyutaḥ sutaḥ
english: At all the full-moon rites, with the ladle raised bearing the oblation of ghee — that fire named Bharata is the second son of Śaṃyu.

sanskrit: tisraḥ kanyā bhavanty anyā yāsāṃ sa bharataḥ patiḥ bharatas tu sutas tasya bharaty ekā ca putrikā
english: There are three other daughters of whom Bharata is the lord; but Bharata in turn has a son, and Bharatī as one daughter.

sanskrit: bharato bharatasyāgneḥ pāvakas tu prajāpateḥ mahān atyartham ahitas tathā bharatasattama
english: Bharata — of Bharata the fire; Pāvaka — of Prajāpati; and the great one, exceedingly harmful also — O best of the Bharatas.

sanskrit: bharadvājasya bhāryā tu vīrā vīraś ca piṇḍadaḥ brahmacārī yatātmā ca satataṃ vipulavrataḥ prāhur ājyena tasyejyāṃ somasyeva dvijāḥ śanaiḥ
english: Bharadvāja's wife was Vīrā, and Vīra the giver of balls of rice; a brahmacārin, self-restrained, ever of vast vow — the twice-born speak of his worship with ghee as like that of Soma.

sanskrit: haviṣā yo dvitīyena somena saha yujyate rathaprabhū rathadhvānaḥ kumbharetāḥ sa ucyate
english: He who with the second oblation is yoked together with Soma — whose glory is that of a chariot, whose sound is that of a chariot — he is called Kumbharetā.

sanskrit: sarayvāṃ janayat siddhiṃ bhānuṃ bhābhiḥ samāvṛṇot āgneyam ānayan nityam āhvāneṣv eṣa kathyate
english: He begot Siddhi on Sarayū, enveloped Bhānu with his rays; he who always brings the Āgneya — he is spoken of in invocations.

sanskrit: yas tu na cyavate nityaṃ yaśasā varcasā śriyā agnir niścyavano nāma pṛthivīṃ stauti kevalam
english: He who never swerves from fame, brilliance, and splendour — that fire is named Niścyavana; he solely praises the earth.

sanskrit: vipāpmā kaluṣair mukto viśuddhaś cārciṣā jvalan vipāpo 'gniḥ sutas tasya satyaḥ samayakarmasu
english: Free of sin, released from impurities, pure and blazing with flames — the sinless Vipāpa fire, his son, is true in prescribed actions.

sanskrit: ākrośatāṃ hi bhūtānāṃ yaḥ karoti hi niṣkṛtim agniḥ sa niṣkṛtir nāma śobhayaty abhisevitaḥ
english: He who effects expiation for beings who are reviling — that fire is named Niṣkṛti; he beautifies those who attend on him.

sanskrit: anukūjanti yeneha vedanārtāḥ svayaṃ janāḥ tasya putraḥ svano nāma pāvakaḥ sa rujaskaraḥ
english: He by whom people suffering pain here moan of their own accord — his son is named Svana, that Pāvaka who causes disease.

sanskrit: yas tu viśvasya jagato buddhim ākramya tiṣṭhati taṃ prāhur adhyātmavido viśvajin nāma pāvakam
english: He who abides having seized the intellect of the entire world — those who know the self call him Viśvajit, Pāvaka by name.

sanskrit: antarāgniḥ śrito yo hi bhuktaṃ pacati dehinām sa yajñe viśvabhuṅ nāma sarvalokeṣu bhārata
english: He who is the inner fire and digests what has been eaten by embodied beings — at sacrifice he is named Viśvabhuṅ in all the worlds, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: brahmacārī yatātmā ca satataṃ vipulavrataḥ brāhmaṇāḥ pūjayanty enaṃ pākayajñeṣu pāvakam
english: A brahmacārin, self-restrained, ever of vast vow — the brāhmaṇas worship this Pāvaka in the cooked-food sacrifices.

sanskrit: prathito gopatir nāma nadī yasyābhavat priyā tasmin sarvāṇi karmāṇi kriyante karmakartṛbhiḥ
english: Renowned as Gopati by name, whose beloved was a river — in him all rites are performed by those who perform rites.

sanskrit: vaḍavāmukhaḥ pibaty ambho yo 'sau paramadāruṇaḥ ūrdhvabhāg ūrdhvabhāṅ nāma kaviḥ prāṇāśritas tu saḥ
english: He who as the mare's-mouth fire drinks water, that most terrible one — going upward, he is named Ūrdhvabhāṅ, the wise one who dwells in the breath.

sanskrit: udagdvāraṃ havir yasya gṛhe nityaṃ pradīyate tataḥ sviṣṭaṃ bhaved ājyaṃ sviṣṭakṛt paramaḥ smṛtaḥ
english: He in whose house the oblation is always given at the northern door — from that the clarified butter becomes well-offered; he is remembered as the supreme Sviṣṭakṛt.

sanskrit: yaḥ praśānteṣu bhūteṣu manyur bhavati pāvakaḥ krodhasya tu raso jajñe manyatī cātha putrikā svāheti dāruṇā krūrā sarvabhūteṣu tiṣṭhati
english: He who is the wrathful Pāvaka among pacified beings — from wrath was born a juice, and then the daughter Manyatī; Svāhā, fierce and cruel, abides among all beings.

sanskrit: tridive yasya sadṛśo nāsti rūpeṇa kaś cana atulyatvāt kṛto devair nāmnā kāmas tu pāvakaḥ
english: He to whom none in the triple heaven is equal in form — on account of incomparability the gods named this Pāvaka Kāma.

sanskrit: saṃharṣād dhārayan krodhaṃ dhanvī sragvī rathe sthitaḥ samare nāśayec chatrūn amogho nāma pāvakaḥ
english: Holding wrath in exhilaration, bearing a bow and garland, standing on a chariot — he destroys enemies in battle; Amogha is the name of this Pāvaka.

sanskrit: uktho nāma mahābhāga tribhir ukthair abhiṣṭutaḥ mahāvācaṃ tv ajanayat sakāmāśvaṃ hi yaṃ viduḥ
english: Uktha by name, O greatly blessed one, praised by three uktha hymns — he begot Mahāvāca, that one with a willing horse whom they know.

sanskrit: mārkaṇḍeya uvāca kāśyapo hy atha vāsiṣṭhaḥ prāṇaś ca prāṇaputrakaḥ agnir āṅgirasaś caiva cyavanas triṣuvarcakaḥ
english: Mārkaṇḍeya said: Kāśyapa, Vāsiṣṭha, Prāṇa and Prāṇaputraka, Agni Āṅgirasa, and Cyavana Triṣuvarcaka —

sanskrit: acaranta tapas tīvraṃ putrārthe bahuvārṣikam putraṃ labhema dharmiṣṭhaṃ yaśasā brahmaṇā samam
english: — performed intense austerities for many years for the sake of a son: "May we obtain a son most righteous, equal to Brahmā in fame."

sanskrit: mahāvyāhṛtibhir dhyātaḥ pañcabhis tais tadā tv atha jajñe tejomayo 'rciṣmān pañcavarṇaḥ prabhāvanaḥ
english: Meditated upon with the great utterances by those five at that time, there was born a being made of energy, radiant, of five colours, powerful.

sanskrit: samiddho 'gniḥ śiras tasya bāhū sūryanibhau tathā tvaṅ netre ca suvarṇābhe kṛṣṇe jaṅghe ca bhārata
english: His head was the kindled fire; his two arms likewise resembled the sun; his skin and eyes were golden-hued; his legs were dark, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: pañcavarṇaḥ sa tapasā kṛtas taiḥ pañcabhir janaiḥ pāñcajanyaḥ śruto vede pañcavaṃśakaras tu saḥ
english: Of five colours, he was created by the austerities of those five persons; known in the Veda as Pāñcajanya, he is the creator of five lineages.

sanskrit: daśa varṣasahasrāṇi tapas taptvā mahātapāḥ janayat pāvakaṃ ghoraṃ pitṝṇāṃ sa prajāḥ sṛjan
english: Having performed austerities for ten thousand years, that great ascetic begot a terrible Pāvaka, creating offspring for the ancestors.

sanskrit: bṛhad rathaṃtaraṃ mūrdhno vaktrāc ca tarasāharau śivaṃ nābhyāṃ balād indraṃ vāyvagnī prāṇato 'sṛjat
english: From his head Bṛhat and Rathaṃtara; from his mouth he swiftly brought forth two; from his navel Śiva; from his strength Indra; from his breath he created Vāyu and Agni.

sanskrit: bāhubhyām anudāttau ca viśve bhūtāni caiva ha etān sṛṣṭvā tataḥ pañca pitṝṇām asṛjat sutān
english: From his arms the two Anudāttas and all the Viśve Bhūtas; having created these, he then created five sons of the ancestors.

sanskrit: bṛhadūrjasya praṇidhiḥ kāśyapasya bṛhattaraḥ bhānur aṅgiraso vīraḥ putro varcasya saubharaḥ
english: The spy of Bṛhadūrja; the greater of Kāśyapa; Bhānu the heroic son of Aṅgiras; Saubhara the son of Varcas —

sanskrit: prāṇasya cānudāttaś ca vyākhyātāḥ pañca vaṃśajāḥ devān yajñamuṣaś cānyān sṛjan pañcadaśottarān
english: — and Anudātta of Prāṇa — these five born of lineages are explained; and he created other gods, the Yajñamuṣas, fifteen more.

sanskrit: abhīmam atibhīmaṃ ca bhīmaṃ bhīmabalābalam etān yajñamuṣaḥ pañca devān abhyasṛjat tapaḥ
english: Abhīma, Atibhīma, Bhīma, and Bhīmabalābala — these five gods called Yajñamuṣas he created through austerity.

sanskrit: sumitraṃ mitravantaṃ ca mitrajñaṃ mitravardhanam mitradharmāṇam ity etān devān abhyasṛjat tapaḥ
english: Sumitrā, Mitravant, Mitrajña, Mitravardhan, and Mitradharman — these gods he created through austerity.

sanskrit: surapravīraṃ vīraṃ ca sukeśaṃ ca suvarcasam surāṇām api hantāraṃ pañcaitān asṛjat tapaḥ
english: Surapravīra, Vīra, Sukeśa, Suvarcas, and the slayer of gods as well — these five he created through austerity.

sanskrit: trividhaṃ saṃsthitā hy ete pañca pañca pṛthak pṛthak muṣṇanty atra sthitā hy ete svargato yajñayājinaḥ
english: These exist in three forms, five by five separately; stationed here they steal — these who are here steal from those who have gone to heaven by sacrifice.

sanskrit: teṣām iṣṭaṃ haranty ete nighnanti ca mahad bhuvi spardhayā havyavāhānāṃ nighnanty ete haranti ca
english: They carry off what those have sacrificed and slay greatly on earth; out of rivalry with the bearers of oblations they slay and steal.

sanskrit: havir vedyāṃ tad ādānaṃ kuśalaiḥ saṃpravartitam tad ete nopasarpanti yatra cāgniḥ sthito bhavet
english: The taking of that oblation from the altar is set in motion by the skilled; those do not approach where fire is stationed.

sanskrit: cito 'gnir udvahan yajñaṃ pakṣābhyāṃ tān prabādhate mantraiḥ praśamitā hy ete neṣṭaṃ muṣṇanti yajñiyam
english: The built fire, bearing the sacrifice on its two wings, repels them; calmed by mantras they do not steal what is sacrificial.

sanskrit: bṛhadukthatapasyaiva putro bhūmim upāśritaḥ agnihotre hūyamāne pṛthivyāṃ sadbhir ijyate
english: The son of Bṛhaduktha and Tapasya, who has taken refuge in the earth — when the agnihotra is offered, he is worshipped on earth by the good.

sanskrit: rathaṃtaraś ca tapasaḥ putro 'gniḥ paripaṭhyate mitravindāya vai tasya havir adhvaryavo viduḥ mumude paramaprītaḥ saha putrair mahāyaśāḥ
english: And the son of Rathaṃtara and Tapas is known as a fire; the adhvaryus know that his oblation goes to Mitravind; greatly pleased, the greatly famous one rejoiced together with his sons.

sanskrit: mārkaṇḍeya uvāca gurubhir niyamair yukto bharato nāma pāvakaḥ agniḥ puṣṭimatir nāma tuṣṭaḥ puṣṭiṃ prayacchati bharaty eṣa prajāḥ sarvās tato bharata ucyate
english: Mārkaṇḍeya said: Endowed with great disciplines, the Pāvaka named Bharata — the fire named Puṣṭimati, when satisfied, bestows nourishment; this one sustains all creatures, hence he is called Bharata.

sanskrit: agnir yas tu śivo nāma śaktipūjāparaś ca saḥ duḥkhārtānāṃ sa sarveṣāṃ śivakṛt satataṃ śivaḥ
english: That fire which is named Śiva, devoted to the worship of Śakti — he is the maker of good for all who are afflicted with sorrow, ever auspicious.

sanskrit: tapasas tu phalaṃ dṛṣṭvā saṃpravṛddhaṃ tapo mahat uddhartukāmo matimān putro jajñe puraṃdaraḥ
english: Seeing the fruit of austerity and great austerity greatly grown, wishing to surpass, the wise son was born — Puraṃdara.

sanskrit: ūṣmā caivoṣmaṇo jajñe so 'gnir bhūteṣu lakṣyate agniś cāpi manur nāma prājāpatyam akārayat
english: And heat was born of the heated one; that fire is perceived among beings; and fire also — named Manu — established what belongs to Prajāpati.

sanskrit: śaṃbhum agnim atha prāhur brāhmaṇā vedapāragāḥ āvasathyaṃ dvijāḥ prāhur dīptam agniṃ mahāprabham
english: The brāhmaṇas versed to the end of the Vedas call it the Śaṃbhu fire; the twice-born call the blazing fire of great radiance the Āvasathya.

sanskrit: ūrjaskarān havyavāhān suvarṇasadṛśaprabhān agnis tapo hy ajanayat pañca yajñasutān iha
english: Agni truly begot through austerity five bearers of oblations here, makers of vigour, resplendent like gold, sons born of sacrifice.

sanskrit: praśānte 'gnir mahābhāga pariśrānto gavāṃpatiḥ asurāñ janayan ghorān martyāṃś caiva pṛthagvidhān
english: When fire, O greatly blessed one, was exhausted and spent — Gavāṃpati — he begot the terrible asuras and mortals of various kinds.

sanskrit: tapasaś ca manuṃ putraṃ bhānuṃ cāpy aṅgirāsṛjat bṛhadbhānuṃ tu taṃ prāhur brāhmaṇā vedapāragāḥ
english: And from Tapas he created the son Manu, and also Bhānu, Aṅgirā — the brāhmaṇas versed to the end of the Vedas call that one Bṛhadbhānu.

sanskrit: bhānor bhāryā suprajā tu bṛhadbhāsā tu somajā asṛjetāṃ tu ṣaṭ putrāñ śṛṇu tāsāṃ prajāvidhim
english: Bhānu's wife was Suprajā, and the Soma-born Bṛhadbhāsā — the two of them together begot six sons; hear the manner of their offspring.

sanskrit: durbalānāṃ tu bhūtānāṃ tanuṃ yaḥ saṃprayacchati tam agniṃ baladaṃ prāhuḥ prathamaṃ bhānutaḥ sutam
english: He who grants a body to weak beings — that fire they call Balada; he is the first son of Bhānu.

sanskrit: yaḥ praśānteṣu bhūteṣu manyur bhavati dāruṇaḥ agniḥ sa manyumān nāma dvitīyo bhānutaḥ sutaḥ
english: He who becomes terrible wrath among pacified beings — that fire is named Manyumān; he is the second son of Bhānu.

sanskrit: darśe ca paurṇamāse ca yasyeha havir ucyate viṣṇur nāmeha yo 'gnis tu dhṛtimān nāma so 'ṅgirāḥ
english: He whose oblation here is declared at the new-moon and full-moon rites — that fire here is named Viṣṇu; and Dhṛtimān — he is Aṅgirā.
